title: THE DAY COUNTER

lines.text: In this town, everybody is born with a number on their wrist.
It's how many days you have left. Everyone can see it.
And you can give them away. Hold hands, say "take them".
People mostly use it for dumb stuff.
Uncle gave his boss a month for promotion. Now he's boss. Seventy-one.
Cousin gave her ex one day to watch him check his wrist.
Coach gave a stranger a year for parking. Now he runs everywhere.
Me? I've got 4,015. Biggest number in my whole class.
I show everyone. I show the lunch lady. Twice.
Then there's my little sister, June. She's four.
Her wrist says 4. Not four years. Four days.
The doctor looks at her wrist and just shrugs.
Mom and Dad want to give, but they're almost empty.
So I go to the town clerk. She reads the rule out loud.
"You can give. You can never take back."
She looks at my number. Then at me. For a long time.
At dinner, I grab June's hands and say it. Take them.
She says, "Take what?" and steals my potato.
She's four. She doesn't get it. She thinks it's a game.
Mom cries into the gravy. Dad stares at his plate.
That night I practise the words in the mirror.
Take them. Take them. Take them.
Next morning, her wrist says 2. It didn't work. Nothing did.
On her last day, I take her to the dock at sunrise.
Her favourite place. The ducks are already awake.
I hold both her hands. I don't let go.
I say it slow, like a teacher. "June. Take them."
And she says, "Okay."
Hers climbs past 4,000. She laughs. She has no idea.
I walk her home. Then I go to my room alone.
Then I wake up. My wrist says 4,016. Same as June's.
The clerk opens the big ledger. Page one. Tiny print.
"Days given away are days spent together."
"You don't lose the day. You only lose it alone."
That's why Uncle never leaves the office.
Why my cousin got one more terrible date.
Why Coach jogs with a stranger every morning.
Everybody gets a number. I just made sure we had the same one.
